properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 9:06AM EDT until September 13 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
FFWOKX

The National Weather Service in Upton has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Fairfield County in southern Connecticut...
Northern Middlesex County in southern Connecticut...
Northwestern New Haven County in southern Connecticut...
Western New London County in southern Connecticut...
Putnam County in southeastern New York...
Northern Westchester County in southeastern New York...

* Until noon EDT.

* At 906 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Waterbury, Danbury, Meriden, Middletown, Wallingford, Naugatuck,
Southbury, Wolcott, Colchester, East Hampton, Mount Kisco, Mahopac,
Lake Carmel, Durham, Sherman, Brewster, Newtown, Hamden and
Cheshire.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Excessive runoff from heavy rainfall will cause flooding of urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other drainage
areas and low lying spots.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area
subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

deaths occur in vehicles.

areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other drainage
areas and low lying spots.

unstable and unsafe.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 12 at 11:05AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Fairbanks Metro Area-Two Rivers

After recent rains, the Chena River is expected to rise through
Monday afternoon and crest around 22.5 ft below Moose Creek Dam. This
level would be right at action stage and those near or along the
river will notice that the Chena is at bankfull. We do not anticipate
flooding from this, but it is possible that groundwater levels rise,
resulting in localized water pooling in typical low lying and poor
drainage areas.

For more information, visit water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc for
the river gage forecast.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued September 11 at 5:05PM PDT until September 13 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Paradise and Hagen burn scar.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast Oregon, including the following area,
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon and southeast Washington,
including the following area, Northwest Blue Mountains.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Paradise and Hagen burn scar 1 to
1.5 inches is expected during the period of the watch. Residents
near the Paradise and Hagan burn scar should prepare for potential
debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of
low-lying areas and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to flash flooding and
debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Meacham, Spout Springs, Tollgate, Bingham Springs, Minam, Ski
Bluewood, Gibbon, Hilgard, Troy, Kamela, Umatilla Reservation and
Kooskooskie.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
